messages.author: e04bb64c7c0b4424
messages.subject: Re: outputOptions function gives an error the first time
parts: The issue is how Shiny loads. When you start the application the tab that the plot is located under is not visible. Because of this, the value that the plot begins with is NULL because there is nowhere and nothing to plot. You need to pass a dummy value to get rid of the NULL passed from session$clientData$output_plot_out_width. Here is the code you are looking for.

library(shiny)

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {

  rv <- reactiveValues()
  rv$plot_out <- FALSE

output$plot_out <- renderPlot({
    if (rv$plot_out == FALSE)
      return(NULL)

    plot(cars, type = input$plot_type)

  }, height = function() {

I hope this helped. Good Luck!

Amber

Glad to hear the it worked. 

You can use a regular variable or even just a constant value in place of the reactiveValue. When I was looking at the program I was originally playing with reactive values for the if else statement. My thinking was to have it be adjusted in an observeEvent function. I changed my mind later on and just never fully removed the reactive value. Sorry about that. 

Sorry about the confusion.

Amber
